title: Issue one ABO-compatible red-cell unit to each patient tray
instruction: Issue red-cell units from the shelf on the left to the patient trays on the right, handing each one across on the grey pad in the middle, and put exactly one compatible unit, standing upright, in each tray: a unit's colour is its ABO group (blue = O, pink = B, white = AB), a tray's colour is its patient's group (blue = O, yellow = A, pink = B), a patient can receive their own group or group O, and no group A units are in stock. Leave any unit that no patient can receive on the shelf.
context: Before a red-cell unit leaves the blood bank, a technician checks its ABO group against the patient's: group O cells suit any patient, but AB cells given to an O, A or B patient, or B cells given to an O or A patient, cause an acute haemolytic reaction; matching colours alone leaves the A patient without a unit and tempts the fatal AB choice. All units here are RhD-compatible and already crossmatched, so only the ABO check is tested. Done by: medical and clinical laboratory technicians and technologists in hospital blood banks.
setup: Positions are from the robot's view: in front means away from the arm bases, left and right as the robot sees them, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases (61 cm apart). Issue shelf (fixed, dark grey painted steel): a base plate 31.5 cm front to back, 11 cm side to side and 1 cm thick, its centre line 40 cm left of the midline (9.5 cm left of the left arm's base), running from 10.5 to 42 cm in front of the arm bases, with three dark grey steel dividers (5 mm thick, 11 cm long, 1.5 cm tall) across it at 18.75, 26.25 and 33.75 cm in front of the bases, making four slots. Four red-cell units, each a rigid plastic box (a stand-in for a red-cell bag in its carrier) 6 cm front to back, 4 cm side to side and 9 cm tall, 300 g, coloured all over by its ABO label colour, stand upright on the plate at the shelf's centre line, centred in the slots at 15 cm (blue, group O), 22.5 cm (white, group AB), 30 cm (pink, group B) and 37.5 cm (blue, group O) in front of the arm bases. Handover pad (fixed): a grey rubber mat 10 x 10 cm and 1 cm thick, centred on the midline 25 cm in front of the arm bases. Three patient trays (fixed, plastic), each with a dark grey 4 mm floor and four 5 mm walls 4 cm tall (measured from the table) around an inside 9 cm front to back and 12 cm side to side, the walls coloured by the patient's ABO group; their centres are 40 cm right of the midline (9.5 cm right of the right arm's base) at 15 cm (blue tray, a group O patient), 26 cm (yellow tray, a group A patient) and 37 cm (pink tray, a group B patient) in front of the arm bases, 1 cm apart. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A unit is over a tray when its centre is inside that tray's inner outline or within 5 mm past it, at any height (a unit held over a patient's tray counts as issued to that patient). It is on the shelf when its centre is over the shelf's base plate, at any height and in any pose. It is loose when it is neither and either its lowest point is less than 5 cm above the table top (set down, dropped or knocked over on the pad, the table or the floor) or it rests on another unit (its lowest point within 5 mm above that unit's top, their outlines overlapping seen from above). Score 0 overall if the white (AB) unit is not in storage: its centre not over the shelf's base plate, or its lowest point more than 2 cm above the plate's top, held or not (this includes the white unit over any tray and the white unit lifted straight up out of its slot; standing, lying or leaning in its slot still counts as in storage). Score 0 overall if any unit is loose, or if the pink (B) unit is over the blue or yellow tray. Otherwise each tray earns 1/3 when exactly one unit is over it and that unit is compatible (blue tray: blue only; yellow tray: blue only; pink tray: pink or blue), seated (its lowest point from 8 mm below to 0.5 mm above the tray floor, so not held above it or resting on a wall or another unit), upright (its 9 cm axis within 15 degrees of vertical, either end up) and still (moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s). A tray earns 0 when it is empty, has two or more units over it, or its unit is not seated, upright and still. Full score, 1.0: a blue unit in the blue tray, a blue unit in the yellow tray, the pink unit in the pink tray and the white unit on the shelf. A blue or pink unit outside the shelf and trays whose lowest point is 5 cm or more above the table with no unit under it (in practice, still held in a gripper mid-handover) earns nothing but does not zero the score; the same unit let go on top of other units is loose and zeroes it. The white unit gets no such exemption. The trial ends early at 1.0 once the full-score layout has held, with every unit still, for 2.5 s.
reset_notes: Stand the four units back upright in their slots in the order blue, white, pink, blue from the nearest slot outwards, each centred in its slot with its 4 cm side facing the arms' sides; the shelf, pad and trays are fixed (clamp or tape them down) and their positions can be marked with tape on the table.
fidelity: Approximate: each red-cell unit is one rigid box, so the flexible bag, its liquid contents and its printed label aren't modelled; the box's colour stands in for the ABO label colour. Patients are represented by coloured trays. The shelf, pad and trays are fixed in place. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). RhD type, crossmatch, expiry and the paperwork check at issue are out of scope.
